title: Adding and Removing Array Elements
learning_outcomes: Explain what adding and removing array elements contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: appending values.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: PHP arrays are ordered maps that can represent lists, keyed records, and nested collections. Keys, missing values, sorting, and transformation order all affect the resulting data. In this lesson, focus on appending values; then compare it with inserting elements. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use adding and removing array elements when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: PHP arrays are ordered maps that can represent lists, keyed records, and nested collections. Keys, missing values, sorting, and transformation order all affect the resulting data. For adding and removing array elements, begin with appending values. Also distinguish inserting elements; removing elements; reindexing arrays. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.
